question: Captio AI or Augio for Danish captions?
slides: Only Danish? *Augio* is built for it.
description: Augio suits Danish conversations, because its own website says it turns Danish speech into text in real time and was built for Danish from the ground up.
Captio AI suits days that mix Danish with other languages, because it captions and translates 60 languages and is made for deaf and hard of hearing people.
Augio's website names conversations between two and three people in an ordinary room as its strength, and says five people talking over each other is not yet a strength.
Captio AI puts each speaker's lines under their own label on one phone, and Recognize voices on iPhone shows the name of a saved person instead of Speaker 2.
Augio's own pricing page says 14 days are free with a payment card registered, then 149 kroner a month or 1,500 kroner a year in November 2026.
Augio lists a launch price of 99 kroner a month or 999 kroner a year for purchases before 1 January 2027, and that price follows the subscription.
The Captio AI free plan gives 100 free credits a day, while Captio AI Plus removes the daily limit.
Augio's website lists computers, phones and smart glasses, and its Danish App Store page shows iPhone, while Captio AI runs on iPhone, iPad and Android.
Augio calls itself a supplement and says it does not replace a hearing aid, a cochlear implant or a skrivetolk, and Captio AI does not replace an interpreter either.
Live captions in Captio AI need internet and can contain mistakes.
